Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the latency numbers encouraging and liked the routing/fallback ideas. A few priorities that came up on our side:

- Main workload will include patient-facing summarization and internal triage (extracted clinical notes) — many queries contain PHI (names, MRNs, dates).
- We need guidance on what to send for a model fit eval vs what must be redacted.
- Target latency: 250–350ms p50 for short summaries (<= 512 tokens).
- Cost sensitivity: we'd like recommendations that balance performance with predictable token costs.

I've attached a short CSV with 50 redacted-ish sample queries the product team pulled together (parkview-sample-50-queries.csv). Compliance asked to loop them in on this thread.

Next steps from our side: we'll aim to upload a broader set (~100–200 representative queries) by next Thursday if you can confirm the right redaction pattern. Also please point us to model recommendations and any benchmark links or eval templates you prefer.

Thanks,

4) A short mutual action plan and dates for a limited eval (100 queries, quality + latency checks).

Recommended starting models (preliminary):

- OpenLlama-13B-ptq — higher quality on longer context but higher resource use; useful if we see longer clinical notes.
- Redwood-8k-safety — a safety-tuned variant if you want built-in redaction heuristics during generation.

Internal links: benchmark snapshot & guidance: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/latency-models-2027Q1 (share restricted). Intake folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBv-parkview-eval-intake

Attaching the prompt capture template and a short intake playbook. High-level guidance below — we'll send a cleaned PDF to ParkView:

Attachment: prompt-capture-template.csv (CSV, columns: sample_id, raw_input, intended_task, expected_output, sensitive_fields_masked)
Attachment: redaction-checklist-v1.pdf

Redaction guidance (examples):
- Remove or replace direct identifiers: full names, MRNs, SSNs. Replace with placeholders like [PATIENT_NAME], [MRN_HASH].
- Dates: convert to relative (e.g., "3 days ago") or replace year/day with [DATE_REDACTED] when the exact timestamp isn't needed for model behavior.
- Free text notes: if the note includes semantic units that are PHI but are required for the task (e.g., medication names), retain them; redact only direct identifiers.
- Hashing IDs: use one-way hashing for MRNs if ParkView needs linkability within the sample set. Store mapping separately in ParkView's secure bucket — we do not ask for mappings.

Edge cases we need from them: long clinical note (>=2k chars), mixed language queries (English + Spanish), user corrections/prompt-chains, and any examples where the user asks for legal/diagnostic recommendations (we need to flag these).

I'll also include a short set of sample prompts that exercise hallucination risk and safety boundaries.

Karthik
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
